chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Asbat from Muhammad ibn Udhayfir from his father who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) gave my father one thousand and three hundred dinars and said to him, 'Trade for me with them.' Then he said, 'Indeed, I do not have a desire for its profit, even though profit is desirable, but I loved that Allah, Exalted and Mighty, would see me exposing myself to its benefits.' He said, 'So I made a profit of one hundred dinars from it. Then I met him and said to him, 'I have made a profit of one hundred dinars for you from it.' He said, 'Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) rejoiced greatly at that, then said, 'Record it for me as the principal of my capital.'
ai.seo_question: What was the spiritual reason behind Imam al-Sadiq's desire for profit in trade?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) entrusts his companion’s father with 1,700 dinars, clarifying that his desire for profit was not for personal accumulation but to demonstrate gratitude by actively utilizing Allah’s blessings (*fawa'id*) in commerce. The Imam’s instruction to capitalize the profit illustrates the Shia scholarly principle of viewing trade as a form of worship and stewardship, where financial success is reinvested to sustain and grow the capital base. This highlights the spiritual dimension of economic activity, where the intention (*niyyah*) transforms mundane trade into an act of devotion.
